observations: Photo 0 shows a used automatic transmission/gearbox assembly resting on a dirty concrete floor, with two people's feet and hands visible holding it.
Photo 1 shows a closer view of the same gearbox casing with wiring harness, sensor connectors, and a small white label/sticker on the casing that is too blurred to read.
Both photos show grime, dried fluid residue, and surface corrosion consistent with a used, removed-from-vehicle part.
A watermark 'NEMZ AUTOSPARE PARTS' appears on both photos; this is the seller's own branding, not a manufacturer mark on the part.
No VIN plate, part number, or Nissan logo is legible in either photo.

claims.evidence: No import documentation, shipping tag, or Japan auction sheet is visible in either photo.
No grading certificate, auction sheet grade, or inspection report shown.
A small label is visible on the casing in photo 1 but is too blurred to read any part number or vehicle code.

risks.risk: Gearbox may not shift or function correctly (internal clutch/valve body wear, CVT belt/chain damage).
risks.proof: A video clip of the gearbox being bench-tested or installed and run through gears/CVT ratios.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not working / for-parts condition

risks.risk: Exact model/fitment (Rogue vs Altima, and model year/engine code) cannot be confirmed from photos.
risks.proof: A clear close-up photo of the stamped part number or VIN-derived tag on the casing.
risks.if_unproven: priced as generic/unconfirmed-fitment CVT gearbox, lowest matching tier

risks.risk: Fluid leaks or seal damage not visible due to dirt/grime covering the casing.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of all seals and the casing after a wipe-down, plus a photo of the dipstick/fluid level if accessible.

risks.risk: Mileage/usage history on the gearbox is unknown.
risks.proof: Odometer photo from the donor vehicle or Japan export certificate showing mileage.

proof_requests: Clear close-up photo of the part number/VIN tag on the casing (the blurred label in photo 1).
Video of the gearbox being tested (manual rotation of input shaft, or bench/vehicle test showing gear engagement).
Photo of Japan export/auction sheet or any paperwork supporting 'tokunbo' and 'highest grade' claims.
Close-up photos of seals and casing after cleaning to check for leaks or cracks.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable by type as a used automatic transmission/gearbox, but functionality, exact model fitment, and the seller's grading/import claims are all unverified from the photos, so it must be priced at worst case pending the listed proofs.
